ordering.ownership: source ownership remains authoritative until the exact target AP acknowledgement matches task generation, owner epoch, target CPU, attempt, sequence, operation, status, error, and result
ordering.wake_and_migration: one blocked wake and two runnable migrations commit only after three unique remote acknowledgements
ordering.dispatch: each AP consumes two tasks from its local queue after one transaction acknowledgement; the BSP consumes two local tasks
ordering.rollback: an APIC-4 timeout leaves the source queue unchanged, withholds target ownership, and rejects the late acknowledgement
ordering.fairness: fixed priority wins; equal-priority tasks use bounded bypass aging with a seven-dispatch hard bound
ordering.shutdown: all eight tasks retire, all four idle owners are observed, scheduler AP ownership is revoked, APs quiesce and park, then 102 pages are scrubbed, verified, and released

nonclaims: PKSCHED4 supports only the frozen BSP-0/AP-1,2,3 legacy-xAPIC QEMU topology; it is not general topology, hotplug, NUMA, multi-socket, or x2APIC scheduling.
The allowlisted AP CallFunction token is a bounded development execution primitive, not arbitrary callback or production capability authority.
No general SMP timer preemption, ring-3 task, address-space switch, per-task FS/GS, full xstate, debug, or PMU ownership is implemented.
No driver or service worker consumes this scheduler yet.
No physical target, N12 exit, release, promotion, or production-readiness claim follows.
